To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
metastatic patterns can be predicted by modelling the dynamics of CTCs on the vascular network and that this requires knowledge of micrometastaic disease.
metastatic patterns are determined by the vascular network topology and the presence of metastatic disease in organs connected by the network.
the metastatic efficiency of a primary organ is a function of both the metastatic potential and the vascular topology of that organ, as well as the vascular topology of the target organs.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing and validating mathematical and computational methods which allow the prediction of metastatic patterns from the primary tumour and the vascular system, and to use these methods to understand the role of the vascular system in metastasis.
the physical mechanisms underlying metastatic spread.
the physical processes governing haematogenous metastatic spread, and how these may be exploited in the design of new therapeutic approaches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
metastasis is the result of the interaction between a genetically programmed cell and a genetically programmed host, with the former being the more important determinant of the final outcome.
metastasis is a stochastic physical process, which can be predicted by the vascular architecture, and which depends on the location and number of micrometastic foci.

the metastatic efficiency is a function of the metastatic potential of a primary tumour and the microenvironment of the target organ, which is a function of its vascular network topology and the existence and location(s) of micrometastic disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
metastatic patterns are a consequence of CTC behaviour in the circulation, which is in turn governed by a combination of biological and mechanical mechanisms.
metastatic patterns are not only a function of the blood flow between target organs, but also of CTC dynamics in the vascular network.
metastasis is not a genetic disease, but rather a physical disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the physical process of haematogenous dissemination is a key factor which should be considered when attempting to understand and predict metastatic patterns.
metastatic patterns are strongly dependent upon CTC dynamics, which are in turn dependent upon the location of micrometatstases.
the metastatic efficiency of an organ-target pair can be significantly altered by the presence of micrometastic disease in a neighbouring organ.
